draft.title: Tests for similar triangles
card: Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size. Matching sides are in the same ratio, called the scale factor.
Triangles are similar if their angles are equal. Two equal angles are enough, as the third must then be equal too.
They are similar if all three pairs of matching sides are in the same ratio.
They are similar if two pairs of sides are in the same ratio and the angles between those sides are equal.
Right-angled triangles are similar if the hypotenuses and one other pair of sides are in the same ratio.
draft.remember: Similar triangles have equal angles or sides in the same ratio.

a.q: Triangle ABC has sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. Triangle DEF has sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. Which statement is correct?
opts: They are similar, as all three side ratios are \(1.5\)
They are similar, as each side is 2 cm longer
They are not similar, as the sides are different lengths
They are not similar, as no angles are given
a.why: Each ratio is \(6 \div 4 = 1.5\), \(9 \div 6 = 1.5\) and \(12 \div 8 = 1.5\), so the sides are in proportion (SSS). Adding 2 cm to each side is a difference, not a ratio, though it is tempting.
a.clue: Divide each side of DEF by the matching side of ABC.

b.q: In triangle PQR, \(PQ = 5\) cm, \(PR = 8\) cm and angle \(P = 50^{\circ}\). In triangle XYZ, \(XY = 10\) cm, \(XZ = 16\) cm and angle \(X = 50^{\circ}\). Why are they similar?
opts: Two sides are in the ratio 2 and the angle between is equal
All three angles are known to be equal
All three sides are known to be in the same ratio
They have a right angle and a matching hypotenuse
b.why: Both \(10 \div 5\) and \(16 \div 8\) equal 2, and the equal angle of \(50^{\circ}\) lies between those sides, so it is SAS. We are not told the third sides or the other angles, so the other tests cannot be used.
b.clue: Check where the 50 degree angle sits compared with the two sides.

a.best: They are similar, as all three side ratios are \(1.5\)

b.best: Two sides are in the ratio 2 and the angle between is equal

problems.detail: "Similar triangles have equal angles or sides in the same ratio" says 'or', which suggests a similar triangle may have only one of these properties. The card says similar triangles have both: equal angles and matching sides in the same ratio. The line also leaves out the SAS and RHS tests, so it is less complete than the card.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct (SSS with ratio 1.5, and SAS with ratio 2). The remember line uses 'or', which wrongly suggests similar triangles have either equal angles or proportional sides, when they have both.

proposal.title: Tests for similar triangles
card: Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size. Matching angles are equal, and matching sides are in the same ratio, called the scale factor.
AAA: two triangles are similar if their angles are equal. Two pairs of equal angles are enough, as the third pair must then be equal too.
SSS: all three pairs of matching sides are in the same ratio. SAS: two pairs of sides are in the same ratio, and the angles between those sides are equal.
RHS: two right-angled triangles are similar if their hypotenuses and one other pair of sides are in the same ratio. For example, sides 3 and 5 against 6 and 10 give a ratio of 2 each time.
proposal.remember: To prove two triangles similar, show one test holds: AAA, SSS, SAS or RHS.

They are not similar, as no angles are given
